items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, the education law, the workers' compensation law and the state finance law, in relation to a strategy to increase participation by emerging investment managers and other minority and women-owned business enterprises involved in providing asset management services, financial services or other professional services
items.lawCode: Amd §§13 & 176, add §423-c, R & SS L; amd §508, add §508-a, Ed L; add §87-i, Work Comp L; amd §5, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6888

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the retirement and social security law, the education
law, the workers' compensation law and the state finance law, in
relation to a strategy to increase participation by emerging
investment managers and other minority and women-owned business
enterprises involved in providing asset management services, financial
services or other professional services


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To create the NYS Emerging Manager and MWBE financial services
strategy in order to allow for the diversification and expansion of
MWBE contracting goals to the retirement, social security, education
and insurance law. This legislation will allow emerging investment
managers under the oversight of the NYS Comptroller the ability to
invest with MWBE financial institutions and to adopt a strategy that
motivates investments in underserved regions of the state.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill would amend the retirement and social security law, the
education law, the workers compensation law and the state finance law
in relation to a strategy to increase participation by emerging
investment managers and other MWBE's involved in providing asset
management services, financial services or other professional
services.

Section 13 of the retirement and social security law is amended by
adding two new subdivisions I and m to read as follows:  The funds of
the retirement system may be invested with emerging investment
managers and with MWBE financial institutions upon such terms and
conditions as the comptroller deems to be in the best interests of the
retirement system.  The funds of the retirement system may be invested
in equity and debt securities of MWBE businesses upon such terms and
conditions as the comptroller deems to be in the best interests of the
retirement system.

Section 176 of the retirement and social security law is amended to
add the terms "emerging investment manager" and "MWBE financial
institution", to specify the definition and function of these terms as
related to what denotes an MWBE financial institution, as defined
under article 15-A of the executive law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Studies have shown that while the State of New York has 8% of all
women-owned business enterprises and 11% of all minority owned
business enterprises in the United States, minority and women owned
business enterprises only received 5.2% of expenditures on state
contracts. In comparison to New York where minorities comprised 40% of
the population, Florida had a minority population of 38% and its MWBE
state contracting expenditures were 25%. Illinois had a minority
population of 34% and its MWBE state contracting expenditures were
22%. This is an attempt to redress this imbalance.  Such data
demonstrates that despite having one of the largest minority
populations and supporting 22 year effort to increase opportunities
for minority and women owned business enterprises, the state of New
York has not matched other states in contracting expenditures with
MWBE's.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
 None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
90 days after it becomes law.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6888C            REVISED 06/29/10

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the retirement and social security law, the education law, the
workers' compensation law and the state finance law, in relation to
increasing
participation by
minority and women-owned business enterprises

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To create the NYS New York state MWBE asset management and financial
institution strategy in order to allow for the diversification and
expansion of MWBE contracting to the retirement, social security,
education and insurance law.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill contains the title, "New York State MWBE asset
management and financial institution strategy" ("strategy").

Section 2 of the bill contains the legislative findings.

Section 3 of the bill amends Section 176 of the Retirement and Social
Security Law (RSSL) by adding six new subdivisions § 176(4), (5),
(6), (7), (8) and (9) which defines the terms "MWBE asset manager",
"minority group member", "MWBE", "MWBE financial institution",
"fiduciary controlled entities" and "best execution".

Section 4 of the bill amends and adds a new Section 423-c to the RSSL,
which provides authorization for the establishment of the MWBE asset
management and financial institution strategy. Such authorization is
within the discretion of the comptroller subject to his fiduciary
duties and obligations as the sole trustee of the common retirement
fund (CRF). Authorizes among other things, the establishment of
reasonable utilization goals for the investing of CRF assets,
conducting of trades of public equity and fixed-income securities as
well as the allocation of investments through equities, debt
securities and special programs involving MWBE asset managers. Also
provides, for the awarding of contracts for financial and
professional services to MWBE firms. The bill authorizes the
comptroller to advertise available opportunities pursuant to the
strategy, work with other funds to create a database and hold a
conference to promote the strategy. There is a requirement of an
annual report to the governor and legislature with respect to the
participation of MWBEs. The comptroller is also required to establish
a certification process for MWBEs along with guidelines for purposes
of identification and reporting.

Section 5 of the bill amends and adds a new section 508-a to the
Education Law which subject to the discretion, fiduciary duties and

obligations of the board of the New York State Teachers Retirement
System (TRS) authorizes the establishment of the strategy. Such
authorization is within the discretion of the board of trustees
subject to their fiduciary duties and obligations as the trustees of
the TRS. Authorizes among other things the establishment of
reasonable utilization goals for the investing of TRS assets,
conducting of trades of public equity and fixed income securities as
well as the allocation of investments through equities, debt
securities and special programs involving MWBE asset managers. Also
provides, for the awarding of contracts for financial and
professional services to MWBE firms. The bill authorizes the board to
advertise available opportunities pursuant to the strategy, work with
other funds to create a database and hold a conference to promote the
strategy. There is a requirement of an annual report to the governor
and legislature with respect to the participation of MWBEs.

Section 6 of the bill amends and adds a new Section 87-i to the
Workers' Compensation Law which subject to the discretion, fiduciary
duties and obligations of the commissioners of the New York State
Insurance Fund (SIF) authorizes the establishment of the strategy.
Such authorization is within the discretion of the commissioners
subject to their fiduciary duties and obligations as the trustees of
the SIF. Authorizes among other things the establishment of
reasonable utilization goals for the investing of SIF assets,
conducting of trades of public equity and fixed income securities as
well as the allocation of investments through equities, debt
securities and special programs involving MWBE asset managers. Also
provides, for the awarding of contracts for financial and
professional services to MWBE firms. The bill authorizes the
commissioners to advertise available opportunities pursuant to the
strategy, work with other funds to create a database and hold a
conference to promote the strategy. There is a requirement of an
annual report to the governor and legislature with respect to the
participation of MWBEs.

Section 7 of the bill amends Section 5(2) of the State Finance Law by
relettering §5(2)(c), (d), (e) and (f) to §5(2)(e), (f), (g) and (h)
and adding two new sections §5(2)(c) and (d) which subject to the
discretion, fiduciary duties and obligations of the deferred
compensation board ("board") authorizes the establishment of the
strategy. Such authorization is within the discretion of the board
subject to their fiduciary duties and obligations as the trustees of
the Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP). Authorizes among other things
the establishment of reasonable utilization goals for the investing
of DCP assets, conducting of trades of public equity and fixed-income
securities as well as the allocation of investments through equities,
debt securities and special programs involving MWBE asset managers.
Also provides, for the awarding of contracts for financial and
professional services to MWBE firms. The bill authorizes the board to
advertise available opportunities pursuant to the strategy, work with
other funds to create a database and hold a conference to promote the

strategy. There is a requirement of an annual report to the governor
and legislature with respect to the participation of MWBEs.

Section 8 of the bill provides a severability clause.

Section 9 makes this act effective 90 days after enactment.

JUSTIFICATION:
Studies have shown that while the State of New York has B% of all
women-owned business enterprises and 11% of all minority owned business
enterprises in the United States, minority and women owned business
enterprises only received 5.2% of expenditures on state contracts. in
comparison to New York where minorities comprised 40% of the
population, Florida had a minority population of 38% and its MWBE
state contracting expenditures were 25%. Illinois had a minority
population of 34% and its MWBE state contracting expenditures were
22%. This is an attempt to redress this imbalance. Such data
demonstrates that despite having one of the largest minority
populations and supporting 22 year effort to increase opportunities
for minority and women owned business enterprises, the state of New
York has not matched other states in contracting expenditures wills
MWBE's.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
None.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
90 days after it becomes law.
